System Commands link

Command Purpose
oflm validate [--json] Verify NPU driver, firmware, memlock, and XRT runtime
oflm add <repo-or-file> Download a GGUF repository or file and register it in settings.json

oflm port Print the resolved default server port
oflm version [--json] Print the installed release version
oflm help Display CLI usage summary
construction
Built-in Registry Migration (#240): oflm add <hf-repo-or-file> already loads compatible GGUF models directly. Built-in oflm pull <tag> shortcuts in model_list.json are migrating from legacy .q4nx archives to upstream GGUFs under #240, and speculative decoding (--speculative / OFLM_SPECULATIVE) is in progress under #189 and #240.
info

item.title: Server Basics
item.description:
oflm serve runs an HTTP server on your Ryzen AI machine (127.0.0.1:52625 by default). Prompts, files, and outputs stay on your device while desktop apps, editors, and SDKs connect over standard JSON endpoints.

Why Use a Local HTTP Server? link

Advantage How It Helps
Zero client NPU setup Apps call standard HTTP endpoints without installing C++ or driver libraries
Shared NPU residency Models load once and serve multiple apps and terminals concurrently
Built-in queuing & streaming Request queuing, SSE streaming, chat templates, and tool parsing run in oflm serve
Drop-in OpenAI switch Point base_url to http://127.0.0.1:52625/v1 without rewriting client code

item.title: Code Contributions
item.description:
Contribute C++ and Rust changes across OpenFlowLM’s inference engines and oflm CLI. Open a GitHub Issue first before starting large refactors.

Style & Performance Rules link

  • Conventions: Match surrounding code: snake_case functions/variables, PascalCase types, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE constants, and _member private fields where already used.
  • Explicit errors: Propagate XRT, file, and dispatch errors with actionable context; never swallow failures or fall back silently.
  • Measured speedups: Record oflm bench or oflm bench-embed throughput across short and long contexts (up to 256k tokens where supported) before and after performance changes.

Engine Subsystems link

Path Subsystem Role
src/open_qwen36/ Open LLM, MoE & VLM Engine Executes manifest.json layer programs and streams GGUF pools (Q4_0, Q4_1, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, Q8_0, IQ4, BF16)
src/open_npue/ Open NPUE Runs batched BERT/BGE/Nomic/MiniLM/GTE encoders on BERT-h* kernel sets
src/open_embedding/ Open EmbeddingGemma Runs embed-gemma:300m GGUF linear projections on npu_matmul_f32 + CPU attention
src/open_diffusion/ Open Diffusion Runs FLUX.2 [klein] 4B generation and editing in one context via full-ELF reconfiguration
src/open_whisper/ Open Whisper Open encoder GEMM + CPU decoder runtime (not yet wired into default export-kernels.py, #240 )
src/src/, src/include/utils/vm_args.hpp oflm CLI & Server Implements subcommands and HTTP routes (no --log-level flag; use /verbose in oflm run)

item.title: Configuration
item.description:
OpenFlowLM separates built-in defaults from your personal configuration so software upgrades preserve your preferences and models registered via oflm add :

File Owner Upgrade Behavior
model_list.json (built-in) OpenFlowLM Replaced on upgrade
settings.json (~/.config/oflm/settings.json on Linux, %USERPROFILE%\.oflm\settings.json on Windows) User Preserved across upgrades

settings.json overlays model_list.json at startup, storing only the settings and custom models you add or change.

construction
Built-in Registry Migration (#240): oflm add <hf-repo-or-file> already registers direct GGUF models in settings.json. Built-in oflm pull <tag> shortcuts in model_list.json are migrating from legacy .q4nx archives to upstream GGUFs under #240, and speculative decoding (--speculative / OFLM_SPECULATIVE) is in progress under #189 and #240.

Precedence, Storage Paths & Server Bindings link

Settings resolve from lowest to highest priority: model_list.json -> settings.json -> OFLM_* environment variables -> CLI Usage flags -> per-request HTTP fields (Server Mode ).

item.title: Docker
item.description:
Run oflm serve inside an x86_64 Linux container with /dev/accel/accel0 NPU passthrough, persistent ./oflm-data and ./npu-cache volumes, and HTTP API access on 127.0.0.1:52625.

Host Prerequisites link

Install the host amdxdna kernel driver and NPU firmware (1.1.0.0+) first so /dev/accel/accel0 exists on the Linux host (see Packages or Nix & NixOS ).

  • Official runtime image (openflowlm:runtime): Bundles userspace libxrt2 and libxrt-npu2 inside the Ubuntu 26.04 container, so host userspace XRT libraries are not required.
  • Custom minimal containers: If you build a custom image without in-container XRT packages, bind-mount host XRT (-v /opt/xilinx/xrt:/opt/xilinx/xrt:ro) and set LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/xilinx/xrt/lib.
  • Memory locking: Always grant --cap-add=IPC_LOCK and --ulimit memlock=-1:-1 so XRT can pin NPU memory buffers.

item.title: Kernel Contributions
item.description:
open_kernels/ holds OpenFlowLM’s MLIR-AIE / IRON designs compiled into .xclbin and .elf artifacts alongside a generated manifest.json interpreted by src/open_qwen36.

lightbulb

Read .agents/skills/open-kernel-pipeline/SKILL.md and .agents/skills/open-kernel-families/SKILL.md for recipe internals and tiling constraints.

Geometry-Driven Pipeline link

Tensor dimensions define a kernel set rather than repository names. Fine-tunes reuse their base model’s compiled kernel set with zero rebuilds; new sizes build via one command; only new layer arithmetic requires recipe or operator code.

item.title: Tool Calling
item.description:
Tool calling lets instruction-tuned models (Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6-MoE, Llama 3.1/3.2, Gemma 4, Granite 4, including oflm add GGUFs) request structured function calls and incorporate local outputs into a grounded answer.

Request Flow link

  1. Declare tools: Pass JSON Schema function signatures in /v1/chat/completions.
  2. Receive tool_calls: The model emits function names and JSON arguments without executing code itself.
  3. Run & return role: "tool": Your client executes the local function, appends the tool result message, and calls /v1/chat/completions again for the final prose reply.
info

See the OpenAI Function Calling guide for schema details, and run oflm-test --tools against oflm serve to verify model conformance.

item.title: Open WebUI
item.description:
Run Open WebUI with OpenFlowLM link

Option 1: Open WebUI Desktop link

  1. Install Open WebUI Desktop and create your local admin account.
  2. Open User icon -> Admin Panel -> Settings -> Connections, disable Ollama API, and add an OpenAI API connection:

item.title: Test Contributions
item.description:
OpenFlowLM verifies changes across four layers: fast CTest unit/smoke binaries, live oflm-test server conformance, XDNA2 operator verification, and static CI verifiers.

Test Suites link

Layer Location What It Checks
CTest targets CMakeLists.txt, src/test/ oflm_smoke, openai_compat, OPEN-VISION-IMAGE-READ, bench_embed, and add_npu_test() fixtures
Live API suite utilities/oflm-test/ Running oflm serve across --llm, --vision, --audio, --embedding, --tools, and --api
Operator checks utilities/build-new-spec.py, open_kernels/designs/ NPU outputs vs. FP64/NumPy references before updating catalogue.py
Static verifiers utilities/ check-settings-ci.sh (flags/env vars) and check_embed_bench_docs.py (published bench-embed numbers)

Running Tests link

# 1. CTest smoke & unit suite
cmake --preset linux-default && cmake --build --preset linux-default
ctest --preset linux-default --output-on-failure
ctest --preset linux-default -R openai_compat -V

# 2. Live server conformance (start 'oflm serve qwen3.5:4b -e 1' in another terminal)
oflm-test --all
oflm-test --llm --tools --model qwen3.5:4b
oflm-test --embedding

# 3. Kernel export & hardware verification
source utilities/env.sh
python utilities/build-new-spec.py --repo Qwen/Qwen3-8B

Authoring Guidelines & Benchmarks link

  • Cover refusals: Test malformed JSON, unknown tags, and unsupported flags alongside happy paths, asserting non-zero exits and clear messages.
  • No external network calls: Use bundled sample assets or deterministic synthetic inputs.
  • Guard NPU-less CI: GitHub Actions runs linux-debug (OFLM_BUILD_KERNELS=OFF) without /dev/accel/accel0; CTest smoke targets must skip cleanly when no NPU is present, and utilities/check-settings-ci.sh catches unclassified flags merged from origin/main.

Benchmark throughput and upload results to the Benchmarks hub (see utilities/oflm-test/README.md ):

item.title: Tool Contributions
item.description:
Python toolchain utilities live under utilities/. Place reusable .xclbin or library inspection scripts inside utilities/ rather than temporary directories.

Utilities Map link

Tool Location Status & Role
oflm-add utilities/oflm-add/ Active (oflm add): stdlib-only GGUF/HF/ModelScope installer, spec_hash kernel linker, and settings.json writer
oflm-test utilities/oflm-test/ Active: live server conformance suite (--llm, --vision, --audio, --embedding, --tools, --api)
env.sh / env.fish utilities/ Active: discovers XRT, ROCm/HIP, mlir-aie, Peano (PEANO_INSTALL_DIR), and OFLM_* paths (env.sh --check)
Kernel scripts utilities/ Active: export-kernels.py, gen-kernel-spec.py, build-new-spec.py, catalogue-add-point.py, register-spec.py
Settings & CI utilities/ Active: generate-registry.py, scan-settings.py, check-settings-ci.sh, check_embed_bench_docs.py
bench-configs / binary-inventory utilities/ Active: sweep configs/logs and precompiled_artifacts.json auditor
q4nx-build utilities/q4nx-build/ Deprecated: legacy .q4nx maintenance only (never add new builders or formats)

Authoring Rules link

Omit compiler or internal hardware jargon (MLIR-AIE, IRON, AIE2P, memtiles, WideDeltaNet, BFP16ebs8, Full-ELF, or XCLBIN) in user-facing prose. Summarize supported operating systems as Windows & Linux (keeping exact OS versions such as Windows 11 for installer and driver requirements), with Packages, Docker, and Nix & NixOS nested under Linux (/docs/install/linux/).

Tips & Current Limitations link

  • Supported encoder tags: The BERT embedding runtime dispatches to the 6 compiled encoder tags in the table above (all-minilm:l6-v2, bge-small:en-v1.5, bge-base:en-v1.5, nomic-embed-text:v1.5, gte-multilingual:base, and bge-large:en-v1.5), not arbitrary uncompiled BERT architectures. oflm pull <tag> fetches upstream BF16 Safetensors directly; when installing a custom GGUF or local Safetensors build with oflm add, pass --name <tag> so it registers under the matching encoder tag.
  • Quantization & loading: Q8_0 GGUF and upstream Safetensors checkpoints load with minimal startup overhead; OpenFlowLM converts BF16, F16, F32, Q6_K, Q5_K, Q4_K, and Q4_0 weights on first load.
  • NixOS package (.#oflm-with-bert): Source-built .#oflm on NixOS omits git-tracked src/xclbins (#244 ); build or install .#oflm-with-bert on NixOS to include the compiled open BERT NPU kernels.
  • Batched indexing & 512-token limit: Pass up to 128 strings per input array for single-pass batched NPU execution. oflm serve returns HTTP 400 for inputs over 512 tokens; use EmbeddingGemma for passages up to 2,048 tokens.
  • Nomic task prefixes (--prompt-name): nomic-embed-text:v1.5 expects a task prefix (query, document, clustering, or classification) via --prompt-name at server startup or prompt_name in the JSON request body.

item.title: Semantic Versioning
item.description:
OpenFlowLM releases follow Semantic Versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, with optional -beta.N or +build.N suffixes).

Increment Rules link

Component When to Increment Example
MAJOR Breaking CLI, HTTP API, or container format changes (post-1.0) 1.2.3 -> 2.0.0
MINOR Backward-compatible features, model families, flags, or endpoints (may include breaking changes while 0.x) 0.4.0 -> 0.5.0
PATCH Backward-compatible bug, accuracy, build, or documentation fixes 0.4.0 -> 0.4.1

1.0.0 marks the first stable public contract; during 0.x, minor bumps may carry breaking changes.

Tips & Current Limitations link

  • Built-in GGUF shortcut & --name embed-gemma:300m: oflm pull embed-gemma:300m already downloads ggml-org/embeddinggemma-300M-GGUF (Q8_0) directly. Because the embedding engine dispatches on the exact tag embed-gemma:300m, always pass --name embed-gemma:300m when registering a custom BF16, F16, or local Q8_0 checkpoint via oflm add.
  • NixOS CPU fallback (#244): EmbeddingGemma accelerates projections with prebuilt npu_matmul_f32 NPU kernels, which are omitted from source-built NixOS packages (#244 ); on NixOS, embed-gemma:300m falls back to CPU execution.
  • Single-query execution vs. bulk batching: EmbeddingGemma encodes one text sequence per pass, suiting interactive RAG queries and 2,048-token chunks. For bulk indexing of chunks under 512 tokens, use BERT Encoders for multi-item batching.
  • Task hints & Open WebUI setup: Pass prompt_name (such as query or document) in POST /v1/embeddings requests or --prompt-name at server launch. In Open WebUI (Server Mode ), open Admin Settings -> Documents, set Embedding Model Engine to OpenAI, URL http://127.0.0.1:52625/v1, API key oflm, and model embed-gemma:300m.

Because OpenFlowLM does not silently fall back to closed engines, pass OFLM_GPTOSS_ENGINE=closed to run the .q4nx shortcuts on Windows or Linux packages (omitted on source-built NixOS per #244 ).

# Run on Windows PowerShell (explicit Closed NPU opt-in required)
$env:OFLM_GPTOSS_ENGINE="closed"; oflm run gpt-oss:20b

/set r-eff high

Tips & Current Limitations link

  • Closed NPU opt-in & NixOS (#244): Both built-in 20B shortcuts download pre-quantized (~14.0 GB on disk; 120B is not supported) and require OFLM_GPTOSS_ENGINE=closed. Source-built NixOS packages omit prebuilt closed NPU binaries (#244 ), so GPT-OSS cannot run on NixOS until #91 lands.
  • System RAM (>32 GB recommended, 64 GB+ ideal): The OS caps NPU-pinned memory near half of system RAM (~15.6 GB on a 32 GB PC). Because the 20B weights and KV cache occupy ~14 GB+, use a machine with >32 GB (ideally 64 GB+) of RAM, or see unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF on the Qwen page for an open NPU + CPU MoE option.
  • Safeguard variant: gpt-oss-sg:20b runs OpenAI’s policy-classification and safety-moderation fine-tune (openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-20b) with identical OFLM_GPTOSS_ENGINE=closed and /set r-eff controls.

item.title: Community & Maintainers
item.description:
Independent & Community-Driven

OpenFlowLM is a free, open-source local AI application and NPU runtime built by the community for AMD Ryzen AI PCs. OpenFlowLM is unaffiliated with and unendorsed by AMD.

Started after FastFlowLM closed its NPU kernels and model converters, OpenFlowLM keeps the entire stack open so anyone with a Ryzen AI laptop or mini-PC can run standard Hugging Face GGUF models locally without vendor lock-in.

Get Help & Get Involved

forumDiscord & Discussions

Ask Questions & Share Setups

Join other Ryzen AI laptop and mini-PC owners to compare models, troubleshoot drivers on Windows 11 or Linux, and share Open WebUI, Continue, and Claude Code setups.
